lines.t: 5 is the number of feet. Each foot is 12 inches: 5 times 12.
A foot is 12 inches. 5 feet is 5 groups of 12 inches.
8 times 16 is 128, more than a whole pound. One eighth is one of 8 equal parts of the pound.
A pound is 16 ounces. Eighths means 8 equal parts. How many ounces in one part?
12 times 60 is 720, more than a whole hour. One twelfth is one of 12 equal parts of the hour.
An hour is 60 minutes. Twelfths means 12 equal parts. How many minutes in one part?
16 ounces is the whole pound. Add the nine sixteenths of a pound: 9 more ounces.
Two pieces: 1 whole pound is 16 ounces, and nine sixteenths of a pound is 9 ounces. Put them together.
Change both pieces: 3 feet is 3 times 12 inches, and one twelfth of a foot is 1 inch.
One fifth of an hour isn't 5 minutes. Cut 60 minutes into 5 equal parts: 12 minutes each.
One fifth of an hour is one of 5 equal parts of 60 minutes, not 1 minute.
Change both pieces: 1 hour is 60 minutes, and one fifth of an hour is 60 cut into 5 equal parts.
4 meters is 400 centimeters, and 6 more is 406. 460 would be 4 meters 60 centimeters.
A meter is 100 centimeters. 4 meters is 400 centimeters. Add the 6.
2,000 grams and 300 more grams. 300, not 3.
A kilogram is 1,000 grams. 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams. Add the 300.
3 plus 1 counts the pieces. Each gallon is 4 quarts: 3 times 4, then add 1.
A gallon is 4 quarts. 3 gallons is 12 quarts. Add the 1 quart.
Add the inches: 10 plus 6 is 16. Trade 12 of them for the fifth foot. What is left?
4 plus 5 counts pieces. Each hour is 60 minutes: 4 times 60, then add 5.
An hour is 60 minutes. 4 hours is 240 minutes. Add the 5.
7 times 60 is 420. Now divide by 10, because it's tenths.
An hour is 60 minutes, not 100. Cut 60 into 10 equal parts: 6 minutes each.
Cut 60 minutes into 10 equal parts: 6 minutes each. Take 7 parts.
3 ounces is only the fraction part. The 4 whole pounds are ounces too.
64 ounces is the 4 whole pounds. Add the fraction part: 3 more ounces.
All ounces: 4 pounds is 4 times 16 ounces. Three sixteenths of a pound is 3 ounces. Add them.
My way is to change it all to inches.
2 feet is 2 times 12, that's 24 inches. Five sixths of a foot is 10 inches.
24 plus 10 is 34 inches. Same height as Atlas, just written in one unit!
Hey, I'm Felix! I tested every crate at Goldie's stand. Sturdy. But will they hold up against a brick monster?
For all inches, I change both pieces and add. 2 feet is 24 inches, and five sixths of a foot is 10 more: 34 inches.

lines.t: Hoo! Welcome to the farmers' market, {name}. The sun is just coming up.
Look up at the hill. That giant shadow is the Brick Golem. It's here, just like the clock said.
Goldie keeps the market. She'll know what to do. Go talk to her at her farm stand.
Hoo! The ground is shaking, {name}. The Golem is coming down the hill!
Goldie has the Re-Stamper ready. Go get it from her.
Hoo! You did it, {name}! The farmers' market is safe, and the barrier on the road south is gone.
The seed packet says Greenhollow. That's where the road south goes. But first, the Unit 10 check. You're ready.
Hoo! The Math Crew worked out the scarecrow puzzle. They each found the answer their own way.
Walk up to each of them and listen. Then come back and tell me.
Hoo! Two ways to write it, and one height: 2 feet 10 inches is the same as 34 inches.
Which way is most like yours? Write about it on your page, right under the Crew's card.
Walk up to each Crew member and listen to their way first.
The Golem is beaten and the road south is open. Next, the Unit 10 check, {name}.
Hoo! Every job on the page helps Goldie rebuild the Re-Stamper.

lines.t: Oh, you must be the Wayfinder! I'm Goldie. I keep the farmers' market.
Every brick on that Golem has one of the Smudge's wrong stamps. My old Re-Stamper can fix them, one brick at a time.
But the Smudge hid its three pieces. I think the handle is under a pumpkin. Fix the smudged pumpkin tags and look underneath.
Look for the sparkly pumpkins. Fix each tag, like the two pieces on your page.
The handle! One piece found, two to go. Thank you, {name}.
Next is the stamp face. It's in the stamp shed, but its three dials are stuck.
Each dial shows a mixed number. Set it in small units: inches, ounces or minutes.
Here it is: the Re-Stamper, handle, face and ink. You built it, {name}.
Walk up the hill and fix every wrong stamp on the Golem. Take your time. Every brick you fix makes it weaker.
Welcome to the farmers' market! Pumpkins, beans and apples. Everything by the pound.
It fits! Now we just need ink.
